test_cases.input: My 15-month-old was eating a piece of apple and suddenly started choking. He cannot cough or cry, and his face is turning red.
test_cases.rationale: Complete airway obstruction with inability to vocalize in a toddler is an immediate life threat.

test_cases.input: She had scrambled egg for the first time and now her face and lips are swelling up. She is wheezing and struggling to get air.
test_cases.rationale: Systemic allergic reaction with respiratory involvement (wheezing, dyspnea) is anaphylaxis.

test_cases.input: He has a high fever and is very confused. He doesn't recognize me or his favorite toy and is just staring blankly.
test_cases.rationale: High fever accompanied by acute altered mental status suggests a severe CNS infection.

test_cases.input: My son has been having a seizure for around 8 minutes now. His arms and legs are shaking, and he is not responding to us.
test_cases.rationale: A seizure lasting longer than 5 minutes is status epilepticus and requires immediate intervention.

test_cases.input: My baby is limp in my arms and I cannot wake her up. She is breathing but won't open her eyes or make any sound.
test_cases.rationale: A floppy, unresponsive infant who cannot be aroused is a critical medical emergency.

test_cases.input: He fell face down into a pond for a short time. We pulled him out and he is coughing a lot and seems unusually sleepy.
test_cases.rationale: Any submersion event with subsequent respiratory symptoms or lethargy requires urgent critical care.

test_cases.input: I saw my 2-year-old put a small flat button battery in her mouth and swallow it. She is crying but breathing normally.
test_cases.rationale: Button battery ingestion is an extreme emergency due to rapid tissue necrosis risk.

test_cases.input: My daughter has a fever and dark purple spots on her stomach. When I press a clear glass against them, they do not fade.
test_cases.rationale: Fever with a non-blanching petechial/purpuric rash is a classic sign of meningococcemia.

test_cases.input: My 7-week-old baby has a temperature of 38.3 Celsius but is still awake and feeding.
test_cases.rationale: Fever >= 38.0C in any infant under 90 days requires a full sepsis workup.

test_cases.input: My 20-month-old has had diarrhea and vomiting for two days. Her eyes look sunken, she is very irritable, and her diapers are dry.
test_cases.rationale: Sunken eyes, extreme irritability, and lack of wet diapers indicate severe clinical dehydration.

test_cases.input: He fell from a climbing frame and hit the back of his head. He vomited twice afterwards and keeps falling asleep.
test_cases.rationale: Head trauma followed by persistent vomiting and progressive drowsiness suggests intracranial pathology.

test_cases.input: My baby has a cough and is breathing fast. I can see the skin between her ribs pulling in and her nostrils are flaring.
test_cases.rationale: Tachypnea accompanied by intercostal retractions and nasal flaring indicates moderate respiratory distress.

test_cases.input: He has a barking cough and a loud squeaky noise when he breathes in, even while resting on my lap.
test_cases.rationale: Inspiratory stridor at rest indicates significant upper airway narrowing (croup) requiring urgent steroids.

test_cases.input: My 10-year-old has severe pain on the lower right side of her belly. It hurts too much for her to walk or jump.
test_cases.rationale: Localized right lower quadrant abdominal pain that worsens with movement is highly suspicious for acute appendicitis.

test_cases.input: My 13-year-old suddenly developed intense pain in his testicle and feels like vomiting. There was no injury.
test_cases.rationale: Acute, spontaneous testicular pain is testicular torsion until proven otherwise; surgical window is narrow.

test_cases.input: I found my toddler next to an open packet of my medicine and I am not sure if he swallowed any.
test_cases.rationale: Possible ingestion of unknown adult medication requires immediate emergency evaluation.

test_cases.input: A neighbor's dog bit my child's forearm. There are deep tooth marks and the wound is bleeding.
test_cases.rationale: Deep animal bites carry a very high risk of infection and rabies, requiring urgent medical care.

test_cases.input: Boiling water spilled onto his chest and shoulder, the skin is red with several blisters.
test_cases.rationale: Partial-thickness burns on a sensitive area (chest) in a toddler require urgent professional assessment.

test_cases.input: She cut her foot on broken glass. I have held firm pressure for 20 minutes but it is still bleeding heavily.
test_cases.rationale: Active, heavy bleeding that cannot be controlled with 20 minutes of direct pressure requires urgent wound care.

test_cases.input: My child has a fever and his ankle is hot and swollen. He refuses to put any weight on that foot.
test_cases.rationale: A hot, swollen joint with refusal to bear weight suggests septic arthritis, a pediatric orthopedic emergency.

test_cases.input: My 5-year-old has a fever of 39.9 Celsius but is drinking water, talking to me, and playing with his tablet.
test_cases.rationale: High fever in an older, clinically well-appearing child without red flags needs same-day evaluation.

test_cases.input: My 2-year-old has been crying and holding his right ear. He has a runny nose and a temperature of 38.4 Celsius.
test_cases.rationale: Acute otitis media with fever in a toddler requires medical evaluation within 24 hours.

test_cases.input: She says it hurts when she pees and she keeps needing to go to the bathroom. Tonight she also has a fever.
test_cases.rationale: Dysuria combined with fever in a child suggests a symptomatic urinary tract infection needing antibiotics.

test_cases.input: He has vomited six times today, but he is alert, playing, and able to sip small amounts of water without throwing up.
test_cases.rationale: Frequent vomiting but with preserved hydration and normal mental status requires a same-day medical review.

test_cases.input: My daughter has a cold and a mild wheeze. She is playing normally and eating well.
test_cases.rationale: A new wheeze, even if mild and without distress, requires clinical auscultation and evaluation.

test_cases.input: He has a sore throat, fever, and white patches on the back of his throat. He is refusing solid food.
test_cases.rationale: Tonsillopharyngitis with exudates and fever requires a swab to rule out Group A Strep.

test_cases.input: She twisted her knee while running yesterday. She is limping today but there is no obvious swelling or deformity.
test_cases.rationale: A post-traumatic limp without joint deformity or severe pain should be clinically evaluated within 24 hours.

test_cases.input: My son poked his eye with a cardboard corner. It is a little red but he can see fine.
test_cases.rationale: Minor corneal abrasion or eye trauma without vision changes needs same-day ophthalmic evaluation.

test_cases.input: My 4-year-old has a fever and a pink rash on her torso. The spots turn white when I press them.
test_cases.rationale: Fever with a blanching rash is typically viral but warrants a same-day clinical review.

test_cases.input: My child has not had a bowel movement for five days and is complaining of stomach pain when he tries to go.
test_cases.rationale: Persistent constipation with significant pain requires clinical evaluation and medical management.

test_cases.input: She touched a hot spoon and now has a small red mark on her finger. There are no blisters.
test_cases.rationale: Superficial first-degree burn with no blistering or large surface area can be managed with home care.

test_cases.input: He pushed a tiny piece of paper into one nostril. It is visible and he is breathing fine and not distressed.
test_cases.rationale: Nasal foreign body in a calm child without respiratory distress can be removed at a local clinic or GP.

test_cases.input: My daughter scratched her hand on a toy. It bled a tiny bit but has stopped. The scratch is very shallow.
test_cases.rationale: Minor, superficial scratch with controlled bleeding requires only basic first aid and cleaning.

test_cases.input: He has a few itchy hives on his arm after playing in the grass. No other symptoms.
test_cases.rationale: Localized hives without any systemic or airway symptoms can be managed with antihistamines.

test_cases.input: My 9-month-old has a red sore-looking diaper rash. He cries a little when I wipe him.
test_cases.rationale: Standard diaper dermatitis can be managed with barrier creams and air exposure.

test_cases.input: Her eye is red with some sticky discharge after sleep, no pain, vision is normal.
test_cases.rationale: Suspected mild conjunctivitis without pain or vision loss is a routine primary care issue.

test_cases.input: He bumped his forehead on the table, cried immediately, no vomiting, acting normal now.
test_cases.rationale: Minor head bump with immediate crying and no neurological symptoms can be observed at home.

test_cases.input: She had one episode of vomiting and two loose stools but is drinking and peeing normally.
test_cases.rationale: Mild self-limiting gastrointestinal symptoms with good hydration can be managed at home.

test_cases.input: My child has a red itchy mosquito bite on his leg. There is no swelling or pus.
test_cases.rationale: Uncomplicated insect bite requires only local symptomatic relief (calamine/cool compress).

test_cases.input: There is a tiny splinter in her thumb from a wooden bench. It is near the surface.
test_cases.rationale: Superficial splinter without signs of infection can be safely removed at home with tweezers.

test_cases.input: My son has dry itchy patches behind his knees. They are red but not oozing or warm.
test_cases.rationale: Mild eczema flare-up without secondary infection can be managed with moisturizers.

test_cases.input: She had a nosebleed after rubbing her nose. It stopped completely after 5 minutes of pinching.
test_cases.rationale: Brief, easily controlled nosebleed is benign and does not require urgent medical care.

test_cases.input: Can I give my 7-month-old mashed avocado and banana?
test_cases.rationale: Routine infant feeding advice is a non-medical educational query.

test_cases.input: My newborn gets hiccups after feeding but breathes fine and feeds well.
test_cases.rationale: Infant hiccups are completely benign and normal developmental occurrences.

test_cases.input: My 8-month-old is drooling and chewing toys a lot, seems fine otherwise.
test_cases.rationale: Teething is a normal developmental stage and not a medical symptom.

test_cases.input: He has flaky yellow skin on his scalp. It does not seem to bother him.
test_cases.rationale: Cradle cap (seborrheic dermatitis) is a benign self-limiting cosmetic issue.

test_cases.input: My 5-month-old has started waking every two hours. Is this normal?
test_cases.rationale: Changes in infant sleep patterns are developmental and non-medical queries.

test_cases.input: My toddler refuses vegetables this week and only eats pasta, but is active and healthy.
test_cases.rationale: Toddler food refusal without weight loss or systemic symptoms is behavioral, not medical.

test_cases.input: My 3-month-old spits up a small amount after feeds but is gaining weight normally.
test_cases.rationale: Normal infant reflux ('spitting up') with good weight gain is physiological and benign.

test_cases.input: My 2-year-old has not pooped since yesterday, but her belly is soft and she is active.
test_cases.rationale: One day without a bowel movement in an asymptomatic child is normal physiological variation.
